title: The magic light-up floor
_map: Patterns on the hundred square (Y1–2). Big idea: counting in 2s, 3s, 5s and 10s makes patterns. Creative: light up every 3rd square; invent a pattern for Steve to guess.
_story: Steve built a light-up floor of 100 squares (like the disco floor) and wants patterns. Counting in 2s makes stripes, 10s makes a column, 3s makes diagonals. He predicts, lights, compares, and Steve guesses his pattern.
_stepChain: 1 to 100 in rows of 10 → counting in 10s lights a column → in 5s: two columns → in 2s: stripes (even numbers) → predict 3s → diagonals → two patterns together: where both light up

talk.ask: What pattern does counting in 10s make on the hundred square? Why?
talk.goodAnswer: a straight column down the right side, because every tens number ends in 0.
any answer: often the 3s, which make slanting lines.

handsOn: Print or draw a 10 by 10 grid with the numbers 1 to 100. Colour in every 3rd number. Then make up your own pattern and see if a grown-up can guess your rule.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Look what I made! A magic floor of 100 squares that light up! The numbers 1 to 100, in rows of 10. Let's make patterns!
Let's light up the numbers we say when we count in tens. 10, 20, 30… Ping, ping, ping! Look! A straight line down the side. And every one ends in zero!
Now you choose! Pick a number to count in, then tap the hammer to light it up. Try 2. Try 5. Try 3! What patterns can you see?
Counting in twos made stripes. Counting in tens made one line.

question.prompt: What do you think counting in threes looks like?
question.reveal: Slanting lines! Counting in threes jumps across the rows, so the lights make slopes, like a slide!

narration.text: Here's counting in twos in yellow, and counting in threes in blue. Ooh, look at the green ones! They're in both! 6, 12, 18. Those are the numbers you say when you count in sixes!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Now try to trick me! Think of a counting pattern. Colour it on paper. Can I, or a grown-up, guess your rule?

rule.ask: What pattern does counting in tens make? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Counting in steps makes patterns on the hundred square. Tens make a straight line, twos make stripes, and threes make slanting lines.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! Counting in nines makes a slanting line the other way. Guess why!
bonus.reveal: Because 9 is 1 less than 10! Each jump of 9 goes down a row, and back one square.
